literal: The anger of those who stood having climbed the hill called virtue, even for a moment, to withstand is difficult.
translation: It is impossible to withstand, even for a single moment, the anger of those great ones who have ascended and stand upon the mountain of virtue.
modern: நற்குணங்கள் என்னும் மலையின் மேல் ஏறி உயர்ந்து நிற்கும் பெரியோர்களின் கோபத்தை, ஒரு கணம் கூடத் தாங்குவது கடினமாகும்.
explanation: This couplet describes the formidable power of the righteous anger of great sages. The metaphor of climbing a hill of virtue represents their lofty moral character and self-control. Although these realized souls are normally peaceful, if they do become angry, their wrath is so intense that it is impossible for anyone to withstand or survive its impact even for a single moment. Thus, the poet warns of the immense spiritual power possessed by those who have renounced worldly desires.
